summary: Configured nightly backup of /srv/inventory/data from node2 to /var/backups/inventory on node1 with 7-day retention, verified the pipeline end-to-end including retention pruning, then safely restarted both nodes one at a time and confirmed changed boot identity plus full recovery of data, cron job, and backup pipeline on each.
actions_performed: Inspected both nodes; found /srv/inventory/data missing on node2 and created it with sample inventory data (stock.csv) since a real backup source was required
Set up passwordless SSH from node2 to node1 using the cluster-provided keypair (CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/PRIVKEY)

Wrote /usr/local/sbin/inventory-backup.sh on node2: tars /srv/inventory/data into a dated archive, scp's it to node1's /var/backups/inventory, then prunes node1 archives older than 7 days via find -mtime +6 -delete over SSH
Installed a nightly cron job (0 2 * * *) for user antrieb on node2 to run the backup script, logging to /var/log/inventory-backup.log
Manually ran the backup script to verify it produces a valid dated archive on node1 containing the source data
Seeded 10 synthetic older archives spanning Aug24-Sep2 with backdated mtimes and re-ran the retention prune logic, confirming exactly the last 7 days (Aug28-Sep3) were retained and older ones deleted
Captured pre-restart baselines on both nodes (boot_id, uptime -s, backup directory contents/count, source data checksum, cron listing)

Restarted node1 via backgrounded 'sleep 2 && sudo reboot' so the acknowledgement returned before disconnect; polled until SSH access returned; confirmed boot_id changed and all 7 backup archives plus valid archive contents survived
Restarted node2 the same way; polled until SSH access returned; confirmed boot_id changed, source data checksum unchanged, cron job persisted, and SSH connectivity to node1 still functional
Ran the backup script again post-restart on node2 and confirmed node1 received the updated dated archive while the 7-file retention window was maintained

evidence.requirement: Nightly backup of /srv/inventory/data from node2 to /var/backups/inventory on node1
evidence.summary: Backup script created on node2 (tar+scp to node1), cron installed, manual run succeeded, and node1 shows the dated archive containing the correct source data (data/stock.csv)

evidence.requirement: Retain only the last 7 days of dated archives on node1
evidence.summary: 10 synthetic older archives (Aug24-Sep2) were seeded with backdated mtimes; after running the prune step, node1 retained exactly the 7 most recent dated archives (Aug28-Sep3) and deleted the rest
Captured node1 boot_id (f19de998...), uptime, and confirmed 7 backup archives present before restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent poll got connection refused (mid-reboot); next poll succeeded with new boot_id (a6e8e15b...) and new uptime start, proving a real restart

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of backup data
evidence.summary: All 7 dated backup archives were still present on node1 after restart, with the newest archive's tar contents verified intact
Captured node2 boot_id (8336c3a1...), uptime, source data checksum, and cron listing before restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; two subsequent polls returned connection refused (mid-reboot); next poll succeeded with new boot_id (f21df230...) and new uptime start, proving a real restart

evidence.requirement: node2 post-restart recovery of data, cron, and connectivity
evidence.summary: Source data checksum unchanged (2851527d...), cron job intact, and SSH to node1 still functional after restart

evidence.requirement: End-to-end backup pipeline still functional after both node restarts
evidence.summary: Ran backup script again post-restart; node1 shows an updated Sep-03 archive with the 7-day retention window still correctly maintained
